newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds and futures comfortably higher in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bunds and futures comfortably higher in late trade.

text.p: German debt prices continued their jaunt higher on Monday with both June futures and cash 10-year Bunds comfortably above the 102.00 level in late trade.

"The German market is well-supported by domestic economics and as soon as things look okay -- or at least not too bad -- in the U.S., then Bunds are happy to go higher," said one analyst at a futures brokerage in Frankfurt.
By 1430 GMT, the DTB June contract was trading 38 basis points higher on the day at 102.11, while 10-year benchmark cash paper was offering a 5.722 percent bid yield at a price of 102.05.

Traders said a strong performance in the French market, which outclassed Bunds after polls showed pre-election gains for the ruling centre-right government, was also lending some extra shine to German fixed income.

On a technical view, analysts said the DTB June future was now targeting 102.18/22 and would have scope up to 102.46 beyond there if Treasuries remain relatively steady in the next few sessions. The contract hit a high at 102.46 on March 5.
But with the potential dangerous may tax estimates due later this week, some analysts said players should be cautious of driving the market up too high.

Economists expect the estimates to show a shortfall of as much as 20 billion marks, leaving Finance Minister Theo Waigel with some hard work to find extra funds if Germany is meet the three percent EMU deficit/GDP ratio.
"The implications of this for the deficit and for EMU are not being taken as seriously as we think is warranted," one analyst said in a research note.
"If Waigel is to find budget savings of this magnitude... he will have to take drastic steps."
If he doesn't, Bunds, futures and the mark are at risk of a swift downturn, analysts said.
